children: The latest inflation readout shows that at least part of the run-up in prices is demand-driven and can't be attributed wholesale to the war in the Middle East, even if some of the pressures are the result of supply constraints, LPL Financial's Jeffrey Roach says in a note. Higher airline fares haven't slowed the demand for flying, with the TSA's travel numbers still running above last year's levels despite rising costs, Roach says. The Labor Department's "food away from home" category is still running hot too, a sign that consumer demand for dining out remains strong, the economist says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)
